perspective:
From Arthur Chung’s available perspective:

- I am Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate. I know Teresa Ortega as a medical assistant and colleague; we collaborate on community service projects.
- During the community service project, I saw Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. I felt concerned and believed she needed help, so I decided to offer assistance.
- I asked Teresa if I could help because she seemed overwhelmed. She said it was kind but she thought she could manage; there was just a lot to do. I said self-care matters and offered to help so we could get through faster together. She accepted and asked for help organizing medical supplies. I agreed and started helping.
- After offering help, I believed Teresa was hesitant because she wanted to prove her capability. I felt empathy for her desire to be self-reliant and wanted to reassure her that accepting help does not undermine her ability.
- I told Teresa I admired her wanting to handle things herself, but accepting help doesn’t mean she isn’t capable. She said she appreciated that and wanted to show she could do it herself. I said teamwork can be more effective and it’s not about proving anything. She said she needed to remind herself of that. I said we’re in this together and I’m there to support her.
- Despite that, I believed Teresa was still struggling. I felt frustrated that my efforts to help weren’t yielding results and wanted another way to support her without making her feel inadequate.
- I told Teresa I could see things were still tough and that she was doing a great job. She said it had been busy and she felt behind. I suggested we work together instead of me just helping her, so we could share the load and be more efficient. She agreed. I said let’s tackle it as a team.
- I believed working together would ease her burden and improve efficiency. I felt hopeful and committed to the collaborative approach. I told Teresa I was hopeful it would make things easier; she said it already felt less overwhelming. I suggested I handle inventory while she manages patient records, with regular check-ins. She agreed and said she was glad we were doing it together. I said let’s make it a productive day.
- I believe our collaboration strengthened our professional relationship. I felt satisfied with the outcome. I told Teresa our teamwork paid off and we accomplished more together. She agreed it was a great experience. I suggested continuing this collaborative approach in future projects. She thought that was a fantastic idea and said we proved we can be more efficient and effective as a team. I said let’s keep it up and I look forward to our next project. She thanked me for being supportive.

I do not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts beyond what she said or what I inferred; my beliefs that she was hesitant, still struggling, or felt burdened are my own interpretations.
